summary: Evidence is direct for long-term-memory failure modes and retrieval requirements, but limited for the proposed Git-backed file architecture: no controlled comparison of versioned small files against vector, graph, or database stores was located.

items.text: Maharana and colleagues, in 'Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents' (ACL, 2024), introduce LoCoMo, conversations spanning many sessions and roughly 16,000 tokens, and evaluate long-context and retrieval-augmented systems. Retrieval improves some results, yet systems remain well below human performance on long-range and temporal questions. This directly supports inspectable retrieval and evaluation, not a particular storage substrate.

Wu and colleagues, in 'LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory' (ICLR, 2025), evaluate information extraction, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, and abstention. The benchmark makes stale-fact replacement and not-found behavior first-class capabilities; it does not test Git-backed records or human maintenance workflows.

Park and colleagues, in 'Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior' (UIST, 2023), implement an observation stream with retrieval, reflection, and planning for 25 simulated agents. Ablations and human evaluations show each memory component contributes to believable behavior, while also revealing retrieval and fabrication errors. The environment is a simulation, so production governance conclusions remain limited.

Rasmussen and colleagues, in 'Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory' (2025 preprint), evaluate a temporal graph intended to preserve changing facts and report gains on long-term conversational-memory benchmarks. It is directly relevant to invalidation and history, but is a product-affiliated preprint and does not compare against a reviewable Git event log.
